Section cdc_child:016 (page 17) is the Appendix table of contraindications and precautions for the 2025 child and adolescent immunization schedule. It contains no recommendation to give a vaccine, so it yields zero rules.

The contraindications are not represented as exclusions for any rule. They are listed in two columns: 'Contraindicated or Not Recommended' and 'Precautions'. The text does not reliably say which column each bullet belongs to, so contraindications cannot be told apart from precautions. Many of them also depend on information structured EHR data would not reliably hold. Examples: allergy and anaphylaxis history, acute illness status, family history of altered immunocompetence, seizure history, Arthus-type reactions, GBS timing, and recent blood products or antivirals.
Not represented, per vaccine:
- Dengue (DEN4CYD): severe immunodeficiency, lack of laboratory confirmation of a previous dengue infection, pregnancy, and HIV infection without severe immunosuppression.
- DTaP: encephalopathy within 7 days of a previous dose, GBS within 6 weeks, Arthus-type reactions (defer until at least 10 years have elapsed), and progressive neurologic disorder.
- Hib: younger than age 6 weeks.
- HepA: neomycin allergy.
- HepB: yeast allergy; PreHevbrio is not recommended in pregnancy (product choice).
- HepA-HepB (Twinrix): neomycin and yeast allergy.
- HPV: not recommended in pregnancy.

- MMR/MMRV: severe immunodeficiency, pregnancy, family history of altered immunocompetence, HIV infection of any severity (MMRV), blood product within 11 months or less, thrombocytopenia history, need for TB testing, and personal or family seizure history (MMRV).
- MenACWY: CRM197 and diphtheria toxoid allergy (CRM), tetanus toxoid allergy (TT), and preterm birth if younger than age 9 months (CRM).
- MenB: pregnancy; latex sensitivity (MenB-4C).
- MenABCWY (Penbraya): tetanus toxoid allergy.
- PCV: diphtheria-toxoid vaccine allergy.
- IPV: pregnancy.
- Rotavirus: SCID, intussusception history, altered immunocompetence, chronic GI disease, and spina bifida or bladder exstrophy (RV1).
- Tdap/Td: encephalopathy, GBS, Arthus-type reactions, and progressive neurologic disorder.
- Varicella/MMRV: antiviral drugs within 24 hours before vaccination (avoid for 14 days after) and aspirin use, in addition to the MMR-type items.
- All vaccines: moderate or severe acute illness, and severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component. Mpox, PPSV23, RSV vaccine and RSV-mAb carry only these general items.

Footnotes 1-5 are not represented. Footnote 2 says a precaution generally means deferral but vaccination might be indicated on a benefit-risk judgment. Footnotes 3-5 are references to package inserts, the PreHevbrio pregnancy registry, and the nirsevimab label.

If other sections' immunization rules are later given exclusions from this table, use computable concepts only where the text is unambiguous. Candidates are pregnancy, immunocompromised and hiv_infection. Even these need human review, because the contraindication versus precaution status in this table is unclear.
No new concept names were introduced.
